title: Sep 11 Results + Sep 12 Preview: Thirteen Wins and Statistical Dominance
summary: Model crushes Sep 11 slate with 13-2 record (86.7%). Tigers top pick for Sep 12.

content.value:
## Quantifying Yesterday's Performance

The model delivered a statistically dominant performance on September 11th, converting 13 of 15 predictions into wins. An 86.7% hit rate over a double-digit sample size isn't noise—it's signal. When you're capturing value at this rate, you're not just predicting outcomes; you're exploiting market inefficiencies in real-time.

## Breaking Down the Variance

Two misses—the Blue Jays and White Sox—don't invalidate the methodology. Both games fell within our projected confidence intervals. The Jays pick at 58% and Sox at 60% represented lower-conviction plays, and regression tells us that outcomes in the 55-60% range will disappoint roughly 40-45% of the time. That's not model failure; that's probability functioning exactly as designed.

## September 12 Advanced Scouting

The model's highest-conviction play for tomorrow features the Detroit Tigers hosting the Colorado Rockies. At 63% projected win probability, this represents our firmest stance on Friday's slate. The matchup features Tanner Gordon taking the ball for Colorado against Detroit's Andrew Sears.

What drives the Tigers' edge? Start with park factors—Comerica plays as a pitcher's park, which disproportionately benefits the home squad against a Rockies offense that struggles to generate WAR outside of Coors Field. Layer in Detroit's bullpen depth metrics and late-inning leverage situations, and you've got a fundamental advantage the betting markets may be undervaluing.

content.title: ⭐ September 12 Top Pick
content.sub: 63% win probability · Sears vs Gordon · Home park advantage factors

content.value:
## The Sabermetric Edge

Gordon brings a concerning FIP trajectory into this start, while Sears has posted better-than-expected xFIP metrics at home. When you combine starting pitcher projections with bullpen WAR differential and situational platoon advantages, the Tigers emerge as a value play even at 63% confidence.

This is where advanced metrics separate informed bettors from casual observers. We're not chasing narratives or hot streaks—we're quantifying every measurable edge and letting the math dictate our conviction level. September baseball rewards this approach as roster depth and bullpen management become increasingly critical variables.
